protein: Spike glycoprotein S, residues 883-1034 scanned (HR1 and central helix)
readout: Cell-surface expression score, higher meaning more S at the surface
assay_method: Deep mutational scanning of S residues 883-1034 in HEK293T landing pad cells, one mutant per cell. Surface expression was probed with an RBD antibody and cells sorted by FACS into four bins; the expression score is the bin-weighted average frequency, over three biological replicates.
remark: The reference sequence is UniProt P0DTC2, the ancestral Wuhan-Hu-1 spike, unmodified, against which all 2,886 mutation labels verify at offset 0. The assayed construct is not identical to it: it is membrane-bound S with the PRRA motif of the furin cleavage site deleted to stop S-expressing cells fusing with each other, carrying an mNG2-11 fusion for the split-NeonGreen readout, and neither the deletion nor the fusion is represented here because the paper numbers its mutations against the full-length wild type and the labels only verify that way. The scan covers residues 883 to 1034, 152 of the 1,273 positions, spanning HR1 and the central helix; the other 1,121 residues carry no mutation and rest on the accession alone. The paper states that both scores were normalized so that the average silent mutation reads 1 and the average nonsense mutation 0, but Supplementary Data 1 ships neither class -- it holds 2,886 missense rows and a single WT-coded row -- and that WT row reads 0.5549 rather than 1. The WT row is carried through as the source measured it, and wt_readout is therefore that measurement rather than the stated anchor. The paper is explicit that a higher expression score means a higher S expression level, and it uses expression as the folding readout by which a fusion-incompetent mutation is judged to be prefusion-stabilizing rather than simply broken, which is why this sits under Stability. The authors themselves note the limit: surface expression here is probed by a single RBD antibody rather than by conformational epitopes across NTD and S2. Not extracted from this paper: the fusion score, which is its own dataset in datasets_virus/Activity; and the Source Data file, which holds chromatography and thermal-shift traces for a handful of validated combination mutants rather than per-variant measurements.
